title: Projection, pressure correction and saddle-point solvers

items.title: Periodic staggered-grid velocity and pressure spaces
items.statement:
Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$ and an integer resolution $N\ge2$, where
$N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and put $h=1/N$. Real scalar and
array operations use the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-field]]). Let
$J_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$; each coordinate index addition below is reduced
to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$
The fixed cell/face placement is part of the definition; collocated central
differences are a different discretization.
items.strategy: State cell and face locations, indexing, all operators and inner products; prove claimed well-definedness locally.

references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 6012–6015: projection, incremental pressure correction, the rotational update, and wall-boundary cautions.

items.title: Symmetric saddle-point system, Schur complement, and block preconditioners
items.statement:
Let $n,m\ge1$, $V=M_{n\times1}(\mathbb R)$, and
$Q=M_{m\times1}(\mathbb R)$. Let $A\in M_n(\mathbb R)$ be symmetric
positive definite, let $B\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb R)$ have full row rank
(meaning $B^Tq=0$ implies $q=0$), and let
$M_Q\in M_m(\mathbb R)$ be symmetric positive definite. The saddle system
and its matrix are
$$ K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B^T\\B&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Au+B^Tp=f,\quad Bu=g. $$
Define the positive pressure Schur matrix
$$ S:=BA^{-1}B^T. $$
In the block-LU convention of [[def-block-lu-factorisation]], the trailing
Schur complement of $A$ in $K$ is $-S$. The exact block solve first solves
$Au_0=f$, then $Sp=Bu_0-g$, and finally $Au=f-B^Tp$; the theorem
[[thm-na-saddle-point-exact-schur-solve]] verifies this procedure and
well-definedness.

For a scaling $\gamma>0$, the pressure-mass block-diagonal preconditioner is
$$ P_\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(A,\gamma M_Q). $$
It is symmetric positive definite. If $P_\gamma=CC^T$ is its Cholesky
factorization with $C$ lower triangular and positive on the diagonal, the
symmetric preconditioned system is $C^{-1}KC^{-T}y=C^{-1}r$, with the usual
change of unknown. This is the symmetric-preconditioning convention of
[[def-left-right-and-symmetric-positive-definite-preconditioning]]. No
spectral bound, Krylov iteration count, complexity estimate, or generic speed
improvement is part of this definition.
items.strategy: Give the typed matrix inputs and output maps; reuse the published block-LU and symmetric-preconditioning conventions.

references.title: Michele Benzi, Gene H. Golub, and Jörg Liesen, Numerical solution of saddle point problems
references.locator: §3.1, printed pp. 14–15, and §10.1, printed pp. 61–63: block factorization, Schur complement, and block-diagonal preconditioning.

items.title: Periodic pressure Laplacian gauge, solvability, and uniform Poincare bound
items.statement:
Use the spaces and operators of
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]] with $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$,
and $h=1/N$. Then $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$ maps $Q_h$ bijectively to itself, the
kernel of $\Delta_h$ on all cell arrays consists exactly of the constants,
and $D_hv$ has zero mean for every $v\in V_h$. In addition, every $q\in Q_h$
satisfies the resolution-independent bound
$$ \|q\|_{Q_h}\le\sqrt d\,\|G_hq\|_{M_h}. $$
items.strategy: Prove the discrete adjoint identity, characterize the kernel by connectedness, and count coordinate paths for the uniform Poincare estimate.

items.title: Second-order consistency of staggered periodic sampling
items.statement:
Use [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]] with $h=1/N$. For a
smooth periodic vector field $u\in C^4(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R^d)$, define
$R_hu$ by sampling component $i$ at each face centre $x_j+he_i/2$. For a
smooth periodic scalar $p\in C^3(\mathbb T^d)$, define $R_hp$ by sampling at
cell centres $x_j$. Put $\|r\|_{\widetilde Q_h}=(h^d\sum_jr_j^2)^{1/2}$ for all cell arrays $r$;
this agrees with $\|r\|_{Q_h}$ on $Q_h$. Then uniformly for $N\ge2$,
$$ \|D_hR_hu-R_h(\nabla\cdot u)\|_{\widetilde Q_h} +\|A_hR_hu-R_h(-\Delta u)\|_{M_h} +\|G_hR_hp-R_h(\nabla p)\|_{M_h} \le C h^2, $$
where $C$ depends only on $d$ and the suprema of the displayed fields'
derivatives through orders $4$ for $u$ and $3$ for $p$. Here the sampling of a
vector field is facewise componentwise. For any $g\in C^2(\mathbb T^d)$ with
zero integral, the cell-centred or face-centred midpoint samples have discrete
mean whose absolute value is at most $C_dh^2\|D^2g\|_\infty$.
items.strategy: Give the exact face/cell sample maps and derive each centered-difference remainder from Taylor's formula with bounded derivatives.

items.title: Exact Schur solve for a full-row-rank symmetric saddle system
items.statement:
Under the hypotheses of
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]],
$S=BA^{-1}B^T$ is positive definite and hence invertible. For every
$f\in\mathbb R^n$ and $g\in\mathbb R^m$, the unique solution of
$$ \begin{pmatrix}A&B^T\\B&0\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}u\\p\end{pmatrix} =\begin{pmatrix}f\\g\end{pmatrix} $$
is
$$ p=S^{-1}(BA^{-1}f-g),\qquad u=A^{-1}(f-B^Tp). $$
The factorization used in this solve is the published block-LU factorization
[[thm-block-lu-factorisation-via-an-invertible-leading-block]].
items.strategy: Prove Schur positivity from full row rank, instantiate the published block-LU result, and verify both equations by substitution.

references.title: Michele Benzi, Gene H. Golub, and Jörg Liesen, Numerical solution of saddle point problems
references.locator: §§3.1–3.2, printed pp. 14–17: block factorizations, Schur complements, and the full-row-rank invertibility condition.

items.title: Pressure Schur equivalence from inf-sup, continuity, and stiffness scaling
items.statement:
Let $V,Q$ be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces with norms
$\|\cdot\|_V,\|\cdot\|_Q$. Let $a(v,w)=v^TAw$ be symmetric positive
definite, and let $b(v,q)=q^TBv$ be a bilinear constraint form, represented
by the matrices in
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]]. Suppose
that, for constants $\alpha,\Lambda,C_b,\beta>0$,
$$ \alpha\|v\|_V^2\le a(v,v)\le\Lambda\|v\|_V^2, \quad |b(v,q)|\le C_b\|v\|_V\|q\|_Q, \quad \sup_{v\ne0}\frac{|b(v,q)|}{\|v\|_V}\ge\beta\|q\|_Q. $$
If $M_Q$ is the pressure mass matrix for $\|\cdot\|_Q$, then the positive
Schur matrix $S=BA^{-1}B^T$ satisfies, for every $q\in Q$,
$$ \frac{\beta^2}{\Lambda}q^TM_Qq \le q^TSq \le\frac{C_b^2}{\alpha}q^TM_Qq. $$
Thus pressure-mass Schur equivalence is conditional on the actual inf-sup,
continuity, and velocity stiffness scalings shown here.
items.strategy: Identify the Schur quadratic form with the squared dual norm of b(·,q), then apply the stated inf-sup, continuity, and energy equivalence bounds.

references.locator: §§3.1–3.2 and §10.1.3, printed pp. 14–17 and 70–71: Schur positivity, inf-sup dependence, and steady Stokes pressure-mass equivalence.

items.title: Backward-Euler incremental pressure correction on a periodic staggered grid
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$, $h=1/N$, viscosity $\nu>0$, and time step $k>0$.
Given $u^n\in V_h$ with $D_hu^n=0$, a mean-zero
pressure $p^n\in Q_h$, and a force $f^{n+1}\in V_h$ whose components each
have zero discrete mean,
$$h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}f_{i,j}^{n+1}=0\qquad(1\le i\le d),$$
define the next step by the following two solves and update:

1. Find $\widetilde u^{n+1}\in V_h$ satisfying
$$ \frac{\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n}{k}+\nu A_h\widetilde u^{n+1}+G_hp^n=f^{n+1}. $$

2. Find the unique $\phi^{n+1}\in Q_h$ satisfying
$$ \Delta_h\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}. $$

3. Set
$$ u^{n+1}=\widetilde u^{n+1}-kG_h\phi^{n+1},\qquad p^{n+1}=p^n+\phi^{n+1}. $$

The pressure is kept in $Q_h$ after every solve; the constant pressure mode
is set to zero. The procedure is only asserted for the periodic staggered
grid and the admissible data stated here. The separate well-definedness
theorem [[thm-na-periodic-pressure-correction-solves-well-defined]] verifies
both solves and the preserved constraints.
items.strategy: Specify inputs, outputs, equations, solve order, gauge, and failure/status behavior; a separate theorem proves the solves well-defined.

references.title: J. L. Guermond, P. Minev, and J. Shen, An overview of projection methods for incompressible flows
references.locator: §3.2, printed pp. 6013–6014: the standard incremental pressure-correction predictor and pressure increment.

references.title: NPTEL, Lecture 5.4: Methods based on Coupling of Pressure and Velocity

items.title: BDF2 standard and rotational incremental pressure-correction variants
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$, $h=1/N$, $\nu>0$, $k>0$, and a step $n\ge1$. Supply
$u^{n-1},u^n\in V_h$ with zero discrete divergence, a mean-zero
$p^n\in Q_h$, and $f^{n+1}\in V_h$ whose components each have zero discrete
mean,
$$h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}f_{i,j}^{n+1}=0\qquad(1\le i\le d).$$
Compute a predictor
$\widetilde u^{n+1}\in V_h$ from
$$ \frac{3\widetilde u^{n+1}-4u^n+u^{n-1}}{2k} +\nu A_h\widetilde u^{n+1}+G_hp^n=f^{n+1}, $$
then solve for the unique mean-zero $\phi^{n+1}\in Q_h$ from
$$ \Delta_h\phi^{n+1}=\frac{3}{2k}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}. $$
Set $u^{n+1}=\widetilde u^{n+1}-(2k/3)G_h\phi^{n+1}$. Choose exactly one
pressure update:

- **Standard incremental:** $p^{n+1}=p^n+\phi^{n+1}$.
- **Rotational incremental:** $p^{n+1}=p^n+\phi^{n+1}-\nu D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}$.

In both branches the pressure is gauged in $Q_h$. Initial values $u^0,u^1,p^1$
are supplied by the caller; no initialization accuracy, stability, or
convergence rate is asserted here. The separate well-definedness theorem
[[thm-na-periodic-pressure-correction-solves-well-defined]] verifies the
predictor and pressure solves for either branch.
items.strategy: Define both variants exactly, state starting-data and mean-zero conditions, and make no unproved stability or accuracy claim.

references.title: J. L. Guermond, P. Minev, and J. Shen, An overview of projection methods for incompressible flows
references.locator: §§3.2–3.3, printed pp. 6013–6015: standard BDF2 incremental and rotational incremental pressure-correction formulas.

items.title: Spectrum of a symmetrically pressure-mass-preconditioned saddle system
items.statement:
Assume the hypotheses and Schur bounds of
[[thm-na-pressure-schur-spectral-equivalence-from-infsup]], with constants
$\alpha,\Lambda,C_b,\beta>0$. For $\gamma>0$, use
$P_\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(A,\gamma M_Q)$ from
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]], and set
$$ a_\gamma=\frac{\beta^2}{\Lambda\gamma},\qquad b_\gamma=\frac{C_b^2}{\alpha\gamma},\qquad \lambda_\pm(s)=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{1+4s}}2. $$
Let $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$ be the eigenvalues, with multiplicity, of
$(\gamma M_Q)^{-1/2}S(\gamma M_Q)^{-1/2}$. Then
$a_\gamma\le\mu_j\le b_\gamma$, and the symmetric square-root-preconditioned
saddle matrix has eigenvalues
$$ \{\lambda_-(\mu_j),\lambda_+(\mu_j):1\le j\le m\} \quad\text{and }1\text{ with multiplicity }n-m. $$
Consequently its spectrum is contained in
$$ [\lambda_-(b_\gamma),\lambda_-(a_\gamma)]\;\cup\; \{1\}\;\cup\; [\lambda_+(a_\gamma),\lambda_+(b_\gamma)], $$
where the eigenvalue $1$ has multiplicity zero if $n=m$. This is a spectral
estimate for the stated scaled block preconditioner, not an iteration-count
or generic solver-speed claim.
items.strategy: Use finite-dimensional symmetric spectral decomposition and singular pairs of the pressure-scaled divergence block; derive the two-by-two characteristic polynomial.

references.title: Michele Benzi, Gene H. Golub, and Jörg Liesen, Numerical solution of saddle point problems
references.locator: §3.1 and §10.1.1, printed pp. 14–15 and 61–63: block diagonal preconditioning and its exact-Schur eigenvalue polynomial.

items.title: Well-definedness of the periodic pressure-correction solves
items.statement:
On the periodic staggered grid of
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], every admissible backward-
Euler step of [[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]] and every
admissible BDF2 step of
[[alg-na-bdf2-incremental-and-rotational-pressure-correction]] has a unique
predictor, a unique mean-zero pressure increment, and a unique updated pair.
Both algorithms preserve the zero-mean pressure gauge and exact discrete
incompressibility.
items.strategy: Test each predictor against its unknown and use the discrete gradient energy; prove compatibility and uniqueness from the pressure Laplacian lemma.

references.title: J. L. Guermond, P. Minev, and J. Shen, An overview of projection methods for incompressible flows
references.locator: §§3.2–3.3, printed pp. 6013–6015: standard and rotational pressure-correction solve structure.

items.title: Mass-orthogonal periodic discrete Helmholtz projection and exact incompressibility
items.statement:
On the grid of [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], let
$\Delta_h^{-1}:Q_h\to Q_h$ be the inverse from
[[lem-na-periodic-grid-pressure-laplacian-zero-mode-and-poincare]]. Define
$$ P_h:=I-G_h\Delta_h^{-1}D_h:V_h\to V_h. $$
Then $P_h$ is the mass-orthogonal projector onto
$Z_h=\ker D_h$. In the backward-Euler algorithm
[[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]], the velocity correction
satisfies $u^{n+1}=P_h\widetilde u^{n+1}$ and
$D_hu^{n+1}=0$ exactly.
items.strategy: Verify range, identity on the kernel, and orthogonality using the discrete adjoint relation.

references.title: J. L. Guermond, P. Minev, and J. Shen, An overview of projection methods for incompressible flows
references.locator: §§2.1–2.2 and §3.1, printed pp. 6011–6013: the Helmholtz decomposition and projection step.

references.title: NPTEL, Lecture 5.4: Methods based on Coupling of Pressure and Velocity
references.locator: §2.3.1, printed p. 45: pressure projection and exact divergence cancellation.

items.title: Modified velocity-pressure energy identity for periodic pressure correction
items.statement:
For one step of [[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]] on
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], with $u^n$ divergence-
free and $p^n,p^{n+1}\in Q_h$, the following identity holds exactly:
$$ \begin{aligned} \|u^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2-\|u^n\|_{M_h}^2 &+\|\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n\|_{M_h}^2 +2\nu k\|\mathcal G_h\widetilde u^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2\\ &+k^2\left(\|G_hp^{n+1}\|_{M_h}^2-\|G_hp^n\|_{M_h}^2\right) =2k(f^{n+1},\widetilde u^{n+1})_{M_h}. \end{aligned} $$
This is a modified velocity-pressure energy identity for the stated periodic
discretization; it makes no bounded-wall claim.
items.strategy: Test the predictor by 2Δt	ilde u, use the discrete adjoint relation, and combine the projection square identity with the pressure increment.

references.locator: §§2.3.1–2.3.2, printed pp. 45–46: pressure projection and pressure update.

items.title: First-order velocity accuracy for smooth periodic Stokes data
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\nu>0$, $T>0$, $N\ge2$, $h=1/N$, and
$k=T/M$ for an integer $M\ge1$. Suppose smooth periodic fields $u,p,f$ on
$[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$ satisfy
$$ u_t-\nu\Delta u+\nabla p=f,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0, \qquad \int_{\mathbb T^d}p(t,x)\,dx=0, \qquad \int_{\mathbb T^d}f_i(t,x)\,dx=0 $$
for every $i,t$. Assume the time derivatives of $u$ through order two,
the spatial derivatives of $u$ through order four, of $p$ through order
three, and of $f$ through order two are continuous and bounded. Sample $u$ at
the staggered faces and $p,f$ at their corresponding grid locations; subtract
the discrete mean from each sampled pressure and force component. Start the
backward-Euler incremental pressure-correction algorithm with
$$
u_h^0=P_hR_hu(0),\qquad p_h^0=R_hp(0)-h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}(R_hp(0))_j.
$$
Then its velocity satisfies
$$ \max_{0\le n\le M}\|u_h^n-R_hu(t_n)\|_{M_h} \le C_T(h^2+k),\qquad t_n=nk, $$
where $C_T$ is independent of $h,k$ and depends only on $d,T,\nu$ and the
displayed smoothness bounds. The estimate is for velocity; no pressure-error
rate is asserted.
items.strategy: Project the sampled Stokes equation, prove second-order spatial consistency by Taylor expansion, and apply the contractive backward-Euler recurrence to the discrete divergence-free velocity.

references.title: J. L. Guermond, P. Minev, and J. Shen, An overview of projection methods for incompressible flows
references.locator: §3.2 and Remark 3.2, printed pp. 6013–6014: smooth-data velocity accuracy and the splitting-order caveat; the periodic staggered-grid estimate is proved locally here.

references.title: NPTEL, Lecture 5.4: Methods based on Coupling of Pressure and Velocity
references.locator: PDF pp. 5–10 (slides 5–10), equations (5.4.4)–(5.4.10): fractional-step projection, staggered cell/face placement, and centred differences; local estimates are proved here.

items.title: Steady MINI Stokes pressure-mass Schur bounds
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be a
bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal or polyhedral domain with a finite,
nonempty conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh. Use the MINI spaces
$(V_h,Q_h)$ of
[[def-na-mini-element-p1-bubble-p1-spaces]], the Stokes norms and bilinear
forms of [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]], and the
viscous velocity form
$$ a_\nu(v,w)=2\nu\int_D\varepsilon(v):\varepsilon(w),\qquad \nu>0. $$
Let $A_h,B_h$ be the matrices of $a_\nu$ and
$b(v,q)=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$ in any bases, and let $M_Q$ be the
$L^2(D)$ pressure mass matrix. Use the symmetric saddle convention of
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]]. With
$S_h=B_hA_h^{-1}B_h^T$, the steady Stokes
pressure Schur complement satisfies
$$ \frac{(C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-2}}{\nu(1+d)}M_Q \preceq S_h\preceq \frac d\nu M_Q. $$
Here $C_F$ is the shape-regularity-uniform Fortin norm bound and
$C_{\rm div}(D)$ is the continuous divergence right-inverse bound in
[[thm-na-mini-element-fortin-stability]]. The result is for the steady
velocity stiffness; it asserts no corresponding bound for an unsteady shifted
Schur complement.
items.strategy: Apply the mini-element Fortin inf-sup bound, the homogeneous Dirichlet strain identity, and the local divergence continuity estimate to the generic Schur theorem.

references.title: Michele Benzi, Gene H. Golub, and Jörg Liesen, Numerical solution of saddle point problems
references.locator: §§3.1–3.2 and §10.1.3, printed pp. 14–17 and 70–71: steady Stokes Schur complement and pressure-mass scaling under inf-sup stability.

references.title: J. L. Guermond, P. Minev, and J. Shen, An overview of projection methods for incompressible flows
references.locator: §8, printed pp. 6030–6032: the role of the discrete inf-sup condition; the steady MINI mass-Schur estimate is derived here from the stated Fortin bound.

items.title: MINI Stokes block-preconditioned spectral intervals
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses of
[[cor-na-mini-element-pressure-mass-schur-bounds]]. Precondition the steady
MINI saddle system symmetrically with
$P=\operatorname{diag}(A_h,\nu^{-1}M_Q)$, using the convention of
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]]. Put
$$ c_-=(C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-2}/(1+d),\qquad c_+=d, \qquad \lambda_\pm(s)=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{1+4s}}2. $$
Every eigenvalue of the Cholesky-symmetrically preconditioned matrix lies in
$$ [\lambda_-(c_+),\lambda_-(c_-)]\;\cup\;\{1\}\;\cup\; [\lambda_+(c_-),\lambda_+(c_+)], $$
where $1$ has multiplicity $\dim V_h-\dim Q_h$ (zero when the dimensions
are equal). This interval is for the steady Stokes scaling $\gamma=1/\nu$;
it is not an iteration-count or solver-speed guarantee.
items.strategy: Substitute the proved mini-element Schur bounds into the general block spectrum theorem and state the resulting intervals.

references.title: Michele Benzi, Gene H. Golub, and Jörg Liesen, Numerical solution of saddle point problems
references.locator: §10.1.1 and §10.1.3, printed pp. 61–63 and 70–71: symmetric block-diagonal eigenvalues and steady Stokes mass-Schur equivalence.

title: Projection, pressure correction and saddle-point solvers — Examples

items.title: A Neumann pressure correction can break tangential no-slip
items.statement:
On the channel $\Omega=\mathbb T\times(0,1)$, with periodic coordinate
$x\in\mathbb T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ and wall coordinate $y$, consider the
smooth tentative velocity
$$ \widetilde u(x,y)=(\cos(2\pi x)y(1-y),0). $$
The field need not be divergence-free; it is zero on both walls. Apply the
unit-step pressure projection that solves
$$ \Delta\phi=\nabla\cdot\widetilde u,\qquad \partial_y\phi(x,0)=\partial_y\phi(x,1)=0, $$
periodically in $x$, and sets $u=\widetilde u-\nabla\phi$. The corrected
normal velocity is zero at each wall, but its tangential velocity at $(0,0)$
is $-2\pi g(0)\ne0$, where
$$ g(0)=\frac{2\pi}{(2\pi)^4}\left(2\pi\coth\pi-2\right)>0. $$
Thus this pressure boundary condition does not preserve tangential no-slip
for this field. The example asserts no convergence rate.
items.strategy: Solve the scalar Neumann Poisson equation exactly for a smooth Fourier mode and evaluate the tangential correction at the wall.

items.title: A collocated central gradient misses an alternating pressure mode
items.statement:
Use the periodic index set $J_N$ and $h=1/N$ from
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], but put pressure and
velocity components at the same cell centres and define the collocated
centred pressure gradient by
$$ (G_cq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_{j-e_i}}{2h}. $$
If $N$ is even, then the nonconstant, zero-mean array
$q_j=(-1)^{j_1}$ satisfies $G_cq=0$. Thus this collocated central gradient
cannot distinguish this pressure from a constant; the staggered gradient
defined on the A page is a different operator.
items.strategy: Evaluate the centered difference at every index and verify the checkerboard has zero discrete mean.

items.title: A scalar saddle system has golden-ratio preconditioned eigenvalues
items.statement:
Take $A=[1]$, $B=[1]$, $M_Q=[1]$, and $\gamma=1$ in the symmetric
saddle-point and block-preconditioning convention of
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]]. Interpret
$V=Q=\mathbb R$ with Euclidean norms, $a(v,w)=vw$, and $b(v,q)=qv$; thus the
pressure-Schur hypotheses hold with $\alpha=\Lambda=C_b=\beta=1$. Then
$$ K=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_1=I. $$
The symmetrically preconditioned eigenvalues are
$$ \frac{1-\sqrt5}{2},\qquad\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}. $$
For right-hand side $(1,0)^T$, the unique saddle solution is $(u,p)=(0,1)$.
This exact example illustrates the spectrum only; it implies no solver-speed
or iteration-count claim.
items.strategy: Verify the 2×2 matrix, its determinant polynomial, the block-LU solve, and the two eigenvalues exactly.

references.title: Michele Benzi, Gene H. Golub, and Jörg Liesen, Numerical solution of saddle point problems
references.locator: §10.1.1, printed pp. 61–63: symmetric block-diagonal saddle preconditioning and its eigenvalue polynomial.

items.title: One staggered Fourier mode is removed exactly by pressure correction
items.statement:
Let $N\ge2$ be even, $d\ge1$, $h=1/N$, and use the staggered operators
from [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]]. Put
$q_j=(-1)^{j_1}$, so $q\in Q_h$, and let $\nu,k>0$. Start one step of
[[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]] from $u^n=0$, $p^n=0$
with
$$ f^{n+1}=k^{-1}G_hq+\nu A_hG_hq. $$
Then the unique predictor is $\widetilde u^{n+1}=G_hq$, the pressure
increment is $\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$, and the corrected velocity is exactly
$u^{n+1}=0$. The pressure update is $p^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$.
items.strategy: Use Δ_hq=D_hG_hq and the unique zero-mean pressure solve, then compute the correction exactly.
